fatal_errors: The material is incorrectly treated as a single-phase solid solution; the target alloy is as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The governing intervention—intermediate-temperature aging, particularly at approximately 600°C and 750°C—is entirely omitted.
The proposed shear-band mechanism does not capture L12 ordering, increased APB energy, restricted cross-slip, planar slip, or stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary tips.
The hypothesis misses the central non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition and predicts only generic degradation under severe loading.
No supporting prior evidence is cited.
explanation: The response addresses the broad question of brittle fracture and offers an experimentally observable mechanism, but it does not reconstruct the target behavior. Its high-stress, high-strain-rate, low-temperature conditions are unrelated to the controlling 550–750°C aging window. It also lacks the required controlled comparison among as-cast, approximately 600°C-aged, and approximately 750°C-aged states. The predicted outcome omits maximum embrittlement near 600°C and ductility recovery near 750°C. In-situ TEM could be useful, but the proposed measurements and falsification rule do not discriminate generic shear localization from the target phase-boundary/order mechanism, nor do they test for dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips or exclude impurity-segregation-driven grain-boundary embrittlement.
